## Added

- **The Propose turn can no longer implement and ship the change.** Two end-to-end benchmark runs
  wrote implementation code out of the Propose turn, archived the change themselves, and finished
  with no approval. The prompt said "planning artifacts only"; nothing enforced it. After Propose
  fires, Readyset now snapshots the working tree and stops with an error if anything outside
  `readyset/changes/<id>/` and `.ai/brainstorms/` changed, or if the change directory moved into
  `archive/` on its own. The violation is written to `CONTEXT.md` naming the exact paths, and **no
  review gate is offered** — the run is over. Readyset never implements without approval, and that
  is now structural rather than a request in a prompt.
- **`--phase-model <phase>=<spec>`** (repeatable), plus `readyset.model.phases.<phase>` in config —
  run individual phases on a cheaper model. Resolved per phase as **flag > config > run pin**, for
  `grill|explore|propose|apply|review` (Refine rides the propose override). An override that fails
  to resolve or pin warns and falls back to the run model: a phase model is a cost optimization,
  never a reason to stop the run.
- **A scope contract.** `proposal.md` now carries a `## Files This Change Will Touch` section — an
  exhaustive repo-relative list — and the review gate checks the working tree against it, showing
  **match / OUT OF SCOPE / unknown**. Paths under `readyset/` and `.ai/brainstorms/` are always in
  scope; an absent section reads as "no contract", never a silent pass. It **warns, never blocks**,
  so approval happens with your eyes open.
- **Per-phase wall-clock budgets** (default 20 min for Explore and Propose). The turn budget counts
  fired turns, but a single turn can churn millions of tokens in tool calls without spending more
  of it — one run's Explore alone was 51% of a 17.6M-token run. Elapsed time is recorded in
  `CONTEXT.md`, and a breach warns visibly instead of failing silently.
- **`--lane fast|full`**, and the lane is now a real run input. Grilling proposes a lane with a
  one-line reason and you pick; the flag forces it for the run (flag wins over the brainstorm's
  recorded lane); the picker shows the effective lane before anything runs. **Fast lane folds
  Explore into Propose** (no separate turn; targeted reads noted inline), caps Propose at a tight
  plan, and skips mutation-testing-style review probes. Full lane is byte-identical to before. The
  lane trims *volume*, never the questions that change behavior.

## Changed

- **Approve & Execute now compacts before implementing.** Explore/Propose context dominated Apply
  and Review cost while everything those phases produced is already persisted to disk, so Apply
  re-reads the artifacts instead of paying for the same history twice. **`Approve & Compact` is
  replaced by `Approve & Execute, keep context`** — the same escape hatch in the other direction,
  for when discussion nuance didn't make it into the artifacts. Sidebar CTAs move from `A/C/R/D` to
  `A/K/R/D`; `compact` is still accepted from older sidebar builds, and a missing or failed
  `ctx.compact` degrades to plain execution.
- **The review gate is fail-closed.** "Discard" is now the first option in the classic menu, and
  nothing runs unless an Approve option is deliberately picked. Previously "Approve & Execute" was
  first and relied on falsy or missing selections falling through to discard — safe only while
  every host resolves a selection explicitly.
- **Grilling researches once up front, not every round.** One session made 17 bash + 16 read calls
  spread across rounds for what one upfront pass covers; rounds already batch up to 4 questions, so
  the cost was per-round research, not round count. Rounds, options, and the no-passive-answer rule
  are unchanged.
- **Acceptance criteria whose THEN can't be observed are now flagged.** A run shipped "WHEN
  src/registry.ts is inspected THEN it contains no direct filesystem calls" and validation passed
  it, though no test could ever check it. `validateChange` now requires each requirement's THEN to
  name an externally checkable signal — exit code, stdout/stderr, HTTP status, file content, a
  command result. Still a *structural* check, and the summary keeps its `(structural check)`
  suffix.
- **The code-review turn checks behavior, not the test suite.** One run's own test asserted the bug
  it introduced, so "do the tests pass" would have confirmed it. Review now checks scenario
  conformance against the WHEN/THEN behavior — run the code, read the diff, exercise the endpoint —
  and distrusts any expected value that could only have come from the implementation under review.
- **Docs say only what the measurements support.** Two independent benchmarks measured Readyset's
  plans as no better grounded than a single read-only pass (~50% in blind judging, twice). The
  README and GUIDE now describe `EXPLORATION.md` as an **auditable trail**, not a quality
  guarantee, and "fresh-context code review" is gone — the review turn shares the session context
  (omp's extension API offers no subagent or detached-turn surface), so the docs say "separate turn
  with adversarial framing", which is the actual mitigation. The Propose prompt now requires every
  repo claim to anchor to a numbered exploration entry or a "verified during planning" note.

## Fixed

- **The gate invariant and the scope check no longer flag pre-existing repo state as this change's
  own.** The helper feeding both never diffed against a baseline — it was a raw `git status` read —
  so any file dirty for unrelated reasons (a WIP edit elsewhere, an untracked scratch note) got
  misattributed to the current change: a hard stop at the gate for a run that behaved perfectly, or
  a false OUT-OF-SCOPE warning on every gate render. What was already dirty is now captured once,
  right after the change directory is scaffolded (first capture wins; never widened), and stored
  inside `CONTEXT.md` so it rides the existing append path and archives with the change. Changes
  with no baseline keep the old behavior rather than crashing.
- **The baseline survives later `CONTEXT.md` writes.** The baseline JSON is parsed between the
  fence markers the writer itself created, instead of from the first `{` to the last `}` in the
  rest of the file. That "last brace" scan broke the moment anything appended later contained a `}`
  — and Refine appends raw user feedback verbatim, so *"make it return `{status:'ok'}`"* silently
  emptied the baseline and restored the bug above for the rest of the run, with no visible error.

## Install / Update

```
npx readyset-flow install
npx readyset-flow update
```
or with `bunx` in place of `npx`.

The extension module is referenced in place, so updating the package is enough — no re-install
needed.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/fresp/readyset-flow/compare/0.11.2...0.12.0
